method_summary: Bounds and empirically probes how SGD sensitivity depends on step count, learning rate, and when a changed example is encountered.
claim_boundary: The smoothness assumptions and simple experimental models do not hold exactly for YOLO training.
stage1_implication: Record realized exposure and optimizer steps; identical configured replay weight need not imply identical optimization impact.

title: Deep Learning on a Data Diet: Finding Important Examples Early in Training
method_summary: Scores examples early using expected gradient norm or prediction-error norm and evaluates data pruning across architectures.
claim_boundary: Importance for pruning average accuracy is not equivalent to beneficial replay at an FN-constrained operating point.
stage1_implication: Keep EL2N and GraNd as preregistered baselines; require paired-seed operational validation before promotion.

title: Prioritized Training on Points that are Learnable, Worth Learning, and not yet Learnt
method_summary: Selects examples estimated to reduce generalization loss by discounting points that are hard because they are noisy or unlearnable.
claim_boundary: Its objective is average holdout loss, not the asymmetric Stage1 weak-defect and difficult-normal frontier.
stage1_implication: Test reducible loss only in a bounded pilot; existing OOF probabilities do not reconstruct the independent irreducible-loss model.

title: Dataset Cartography: Mapping and Diagnosing Datasets with Training Dynamics
method_summary: Builds data maps from per-example confidence and variability and compares subsets across in-domain and out-of-domain tests.
claim_boundary: The original NLP buckets are model-relative and should not be treated as universal Stage1 value classes.
stage1_implication: Define easy, ambiguous, and hard-to-learn strata descriptively, then test replay effects within each stratum.

title: An Empirical Study of Example Forgetting during Deep Neural Network Learning
method_summary: Counts forgetting events from correctness transitions and studies the effect of removing unforgettable examples.
claim_boundary: Forgetting depends on model and training recipe and does not encode the direction of an operational-tail update.
stage1_implication: Use forgetting as a reproducible sample descriptor and test its interaction with seed, not as a final value label.

title: A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks
method_summary: Contrasts optimization on real and noise data and finds that deep networks tend to learn simple patterns before memorizing noise.
claim_boundary: Population-level memorization behavior does not identify whether replaying one Stage1 sample helps the protected tail.
stage1_implication: Separate early learnability from late memorization before calling persistent hard samples valuable.

title: Distributional Training Data Attribution: What do Influence Functions Sample?
method_summary: Defines attribution for stochastic training as the dependence of an output distribution on the training dataset and evaluates distribution-aware pruning.
claim_boundary: The demonstrated pruning tasks do not establish the number of seeds needed for Stage1's constrained operating frontier.
stage1_implication: Estimate arm effects and sample-set effects over seeds, including variance and tail-risk, instead of only the mean.

title: A Bayesian Approach To Analysing Training Data Attribution In Deep Learning
method_summary: Treats learned models and attribution estimates as random variables and tests whether sample influence survives initialization and mini-batch noise.
claim_boundary: The paper warns that noise-independent influential pairs are rare; it does not provide a cheap scalar ranking for Stage1.
stage1_implication: Treat the 23 same-selection seed reversals as a distributional effect, not ranking noise to average away.
